```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(EpiExposure)
library(dlnm)
---

## 1. Motivation

Distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs) are widely used to quantify
exposure–lag–response associations. However, applied epidemiological studies
require additional methodological structure to support interpretation,
including biologically meaningful exposure windows and standardised summaries.

The **EpiExposure** package was developed to address this gap.

---

## 2. Defining epidemiological exposure

```r
exp <- define_exposure(
  data   = weather,
  vars   = c("tmean"),
  lag    = 85,
  argvar = list(fun = "ns", df = 4),
  arglag = list(fun = "ns", df = 4),
  id     = "plot",
  time   = "dpp"
)


fit <- fit_epidlnm(
  exposure = exp,
  outcome  = epi$severity,
  family   = beta_family()
)

win <- define_windows(
  lag    = 85,
  breaks = c(0, 30, 60, 85)
)

eff <- summarise_effects(
  fit,
  windows = win,
  at  = quantile(weather$tmean, 0.9),
  cen = quantile(weather$tmean, 0.5)
)

plot_epi_effects(eff, type = "windows")

EpiExposure relies internally on dlnm::crossbasis() and
dlnm::crosspred(). All statistical estimation is conducted using the
original DLNM framework; EpiExposure adds a domain-specific epidemiological
layer focused on interpretation and reproducibility.
